llm.summary: The skill is mostly a coherent fal.ai connector, but its setup instructions tell users to run an unverified remote installer directly in a shell.

dimensions.detail: Installing a CLI is purpose-aligned, but executing a remote installer gives broad local code-execution authority compared with the otherwise scoped fal.ai connector operations.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documented macOS/Linux and Windows install commands pipe mutable remote content directly into bash or PowerShell without version pinning, checksum verification, signature verification, or a required manual review step.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Normal tool scope is limited to Bash(oo *), but first-time setup includes direct shell execution of downloaded installer scripts, which falls outside the narrow connector workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not show hidden persistence, credential theft, or local token handling; CLI installation and OOMOL login are disclosed one-time setup steps, though they can persist local tooling or session state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose and normal actions are coherent: it uses the OOMOL oo CLI to inspect schemas and run fal.ai connector actions, with write actions labeled and requiring confirmation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, do not let an agent automatically run the curl|bash or irm|iex commands. Install the oo CLI only from a trusted, verifiable source, preferably with a pinned version and checksum or signature, and separately approve any fal.ai write actions such as submitting or canceling queue requests.
llm.findings:
[SC2] expected: The external installer is related to obtaining the oo CLI needed by the skill, but the pipe-to-shell mechanism is under-scoped and unsafe enough to warrant Review.
[T03] expected: The remote retrieval and immediate execution finding is supported by SKILL.md lines 60-67; no evidence shows malicious payload intent, but the mutable unverified installer creates material supply-chain risk.
